subject.title: feat: sidebar session state slot, worktree/automation badges, archive disables bound cron jobs

question: After the live projection defect is fixed, should archiving permanently disable bound cron jobs until an administrator explicitly re-enables them, even if the session is later restored?
rationale: The PR deliberately changes an existing session operation into a persistent cross-owner cron-state mutation; tests can prove implementation behavior, but only maintainers can confirm that irreversible upgrade and operator contract.

options.title: Keep explicit manual re-enable
options.body: Archive disables bound jobs and restore leaves them disabled, with docs and UI making the manual re-enable requirement clear.

options.title: Restore prior enabled state
options.body: Track which jobs were disabled by archive and re-enable only those jobs when the session is restored, adding persistent state and migration complexity.

options.title: Do not cascade from archive
options.body: Keep archive and cron administration separate, retaining only the sidebar automation visibility portion of the PR.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit manual re-enable
recommendation.body: Archive disables bound jobs and restore leaves them disabled, with docs and UI making the manual re-enable requirement clear.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current-main history across the affected UI, session, and cron lifecycle surfaces.
